ports.name: i_clk
ports.description: System clock, 100 MHz target; all logic is clocked on its rising edge

ports.name: i_rst_n
ports.description: Active-low reset

ports.name: i_awaddr
ports.description: Write burst start byte address

ports.name: i_awvalid
ports.description: Write address valid

ports.name: o_awready
ports.description: Write address ready. Combinational: write FSM in S_IDLE AND AWFIFO not full.

ports.name: i_awburst
ports.description: Burst type: 00 = FIXED, 01 = INCR, 10 = WRAP; reserved 11 is addressed like WRAP

ports.name: i_awlen
ports.description: Burst length − 1 (number of beats − 1)

ports.name: i_awid
ports.description: Write transaction ID

ports.name: i_awsize
ports.description: Bytes per beat = 2i_awsize; values > MAX_SIZE are an error (F07)

ports.name: i_wdata
ports.description: Write data

ports.name: i_wstrb
ports.description: Write strobe, one bit per byte lane. Only asserted lanes are written to SRAM.

ports.name: i_wvalid
ports.description: Write data valid

ports.name: o_wready
ports.description: Write data ready = WFIFO not full

ports.name: i_wlast
ports.description: Last write beat. Present but not used internally.

ports.name: o_bid
ports.description: Write response ID (the burst's AWID)

ports.name: o_bresp
ports.description: 2'b00 OKAY, or 2'b10 SLVERR if the burst's start address was misaligned to 2AWSIZE or AWSIZE exceeded the bus width

ports.name: o_bvalid
ports.description: Write response valid = BFIFO not empty

ports.name: i_bready
ports.description: Write response ready

ports.name: i_araddr
ports.description: Read burst start byte address

ports.name: i_arvalid
ports.description: Read address valid

ports.name: o_arready
ports.description: Read address ready. Combinational: read FSM in S_IDLE AND ARFIFO not full.

ports.name: i_arburst
ports.description: Burst type (same encoding as i_awburst)

ports.name: i_arlen
ports.description: Burst length − 1

ports.name: i_arid
ports.description: Read transaction ID

ports.name: i_arsize
ports.description: Bytes per beat = 2i_arsize; same validity rule as i_awsize

ports.name: o_rid
ports.description: Read response ID (the burst's ARID)

ports.name: o_rdata
ports.description: Read data (always the full SRAM word)

ports.name: o_rresp
ports.description: 2'b00 OKAY, or 2'b10 SLVERR if this beat's burst had a misaligned start address or an oversized ARSIZE

ports.name: o_rvalid
ports.description: Read data valid = RFIFO not empty

ports.name: o_rlast
ports.description: Last beat of the read burst

ports.name: i_rready
ports.description: Read data ready

ports.name: o_sram_addr
ports.description: Per-bank SRAM byte address: the full, un-hashed AXI beat address. Assumption: 0 when the bank has neither o_sram_we[k] nor o_sram_oe[k] asserted.

ports.name: o_sram_wdata
ports.description: Per-bank write data; valid only while o_sram_we[k] = 1, don't-care otherwise

ports.name: o_sram_wstrb
ports.description: Per-bank, per-byte write strobe. Pass-through of i_wstrb while o_sram_we[k] = 1. Shall be all-zero whenever o_sram_we[k] = 0, including SLVERR beats and non-selected banks.

ports.name: i_sram_rdata
ports.description: Per-bank read data, sampled in the cycle after o_sram_oe[k]

ports.name: o_sram_we
ports.description: Per-bank write enable, active high

ports.name: o_sram_oe
ports.description: Per-bank output (read) enable, active high, asserted in the read-issue cycle (also for SLVERR read beats)

constraints.description: Data width is a whole number of bytes with a power-of-two lane count.
FIFO depth is a power of 2, at least 2.
Bank count is a power of 2.
Address wide enough for the bank hash (BYTE_LSB = $clog2(PARA_DATA_WD/8)).
Address wider than the byte offset (BYTE_LSB).

interfaces.protocol: AXI4 write channels AW, W, B
synchronous SRAM, byte strobes, 1-cycle read latency

requirements.text: The design shall use a single clock domain i_clk; all sequential state shall change only on the rising edge of i_clk or on assertion of i_rst_n.
i_rst_n shall be an active-low reset with asynchronous assertion; its deassertion shall be synchronous to i_clk (synchronizer outside the block).
requirements.status_reason: Assumption at spec.md:77; see OI-001. TB asserts asynchronously and deasserts synchronously, no further check.

requirements.text: The AXI write address channel shall consist of i_awaddr[PARA_ADDR_WD-1:0], i_awvalid, o_awready, i_awburst[1:0], i_awlen[PARA_LEN_WD-1:0], i_awid[PARA_ID_WD-1:0] and i_awsize[2:0].
The AXI write data channel shall consist of i_wdata[PARA_DATA_WD-1:0], i_wstrb[PARA_DATA_WD/8-1:0], i_wvalid, o_wready and i_wlast.
The AXI write response channel shall consist of o_bid[PARA_ID_WD-1:0], o_bresp[1:0], o_bvalid and i_bready.
The AXI read address channel shall consist of i_araddr[PARA_ADDR_WD-1:0], i_arvalid, o_arready, i_arburst[1:0], i_arlen[PARA_LEN_WD-1:0], i_arid[PARA_ID_WD-1:0] and i_arsize[2:0].
The AXI read data channel shall consist of o_rid[PARA_ID_WD-1:0], o_rdata[PARA_DATA_WD-1:0], o_rresp[1:0], o_rvalid, o_rlast and i_rready; o_rdata shall always carry the full SRAM word.

The SRAM interface shall provide per-bank packed arrays o_sram_addr[PARA_NUM_BANKS-1:0][PARA_ADDR_WD-1:0], o_sram_wdata[PARA_NUM_BANKS-1:0][PARA_DATA_WD-1:0], o_sram_wstrb[PARA_NUM_BANKS-1:0][PARA_DATA_WD/8-1:0], o_sram_we[PARA_NUM_BANKS-1:0], o_sram_oe[PARA_NUM_BANKS-1:0] (active high) and input i_sram_rdata[PARA_NUM_BANKS-1:0][PARA_DATA_WD-1:0]; with PARA_NUM_BANKS = 1 it shall be bit-for-bit the single-SRAM interface.
requirements.status_reason: The port set, widths and the single-SRAM mapping at PARA_NUM_BANKS=1 are stated; only reset and idle values carry assumptions, tracked under REQ-042 and REQ-049. Traced by TC-001 and COV-001.

requirements.text: o_awready shall be 1 exactly when the write address FSM is in S_IDLE and AWFIFO is not full (current-cycle flag); o_arready likewise for the read FSM and ARFIFO. Neither shall depend combinationally on the corresponding VALID input, and a FIFO pop in the same cycle shall not raise READY.

o_wready shall equal NOT(WFIFO full) on the current-cycle flag and shall not depend on i_wvalid; {i_wstrb, i_wdata} shall be pushed into WFIFO when i_wvalid & o_wready, and W beats may be accepted before their AW burst.

o_bvalid shall equal NOT(BFIFO empty) and o_bid/o_bresp shall be the BFIFO head entry; once o_bvalid is 1, it and the payload shall stay stable until the cycle where i_bready = 1, when the entry is popped.
o_rvalid shall equal NOT(RFIFO empty) and o_rid/o_rdata/o_rresp/o_rlast shall be the RFIFO head entry; they shall stay stable until popped in a cycle where i_rready = 1.
Response encodings shall be OKAY = 2'b00 and SLVERR = 2'b10; EXOKAY and DECERR shall never be generated on o_bresp or o_rresp.
The controller shall return exactly one B response per accepted AW burst, and exactly AxLEN+1 R beats per accepted AR burst with o_rlast = 1 only on the last beat.
The AXI master shall keep VALID and its payload stable from assertion until the handshake on every AXI input channel (AW, W, AR, and READY-side B/R are not constrained).
requirements.status_reason: Master obligation; the stimulus agent honours it, it is not a DUT check.

requirements.text: The AXI master shall send exactly AWLEN+1 W beats per AW burst, in AW order without write-data interleaving, shall use WRAP lengths of 2, 4, 8 or 16 beats only, and should not use AxBURST = 2'b11.
requirements.status_reason: Master obligation; stimulus sends AWLEN+1 beats, WRAP lengths 2/4/8/16 only and never AxBURST=2'b11.

requirements.text: Each SRAM bank k shall write o_sram_wdata[k] into the byte lanes selected by o_sram_wstrb[k] at word o_sram_addr[k][PARA_ADDR_WD-1:BYTE_LSB] at the rising edge ending a cycle with o_sram_we[k] = 1 (unselected bytes unchanged), and shall present the word addressed in a cycle with o_sram_oe[k] = 1 on i_sram_rdata[k] throughout the following cycle (exactly one-cycle read latency); the low BYTE_LSB address bits are ignored and each bank holds the full addressable range.
requirements.status_reason: SRAM behavior contract is an assumption (OI-003); the TB SRAM model implements it as stated.

requirements.text: In any cycle, o_sram_we[k] and o_sram_oe[k] shall not both be 1 for the same bank k.
The controller shall be an AXI4 slave with independent read and write channels: AW and AR handshakes in the same cycle shall be independent and both accepted when their READYs are 1.

After each pushed beat the address FSM shall keep the next beat address unchanged for FIXED bursts (2'b00) and set it to addr + 2**AxSIZE for INCR bursts (2'b01), using the registered AxSIZE; address arithmetic shall be modulo 2**PARA_ADDR_WD with no 4 KB boundary check.
requirements.status_reason: Approved by the user's answer Q-TB-OI-006.

requirements.text: For WRAP bursts (2'b10) and reserved AxBURST = 2'b11, the next address shall be addr + size_bytes unless that equals wrap_lower + size_bytes*burst_len, in which case it shall be wrap_lower, where wrap_lower = start_addr & ~(size_bytes*burst_len − 1) and burst_len = AxLEN+1 are computed and latched at the handshake (e.g. 4-beat 32-bit WRAP from 0x88 visits 0x88, 0x8C, 0x80, 0x84). AxBURST = 2'b11 shall not by itself cause SLVERR.
requirements.status_reason: Cited as assumption at spec.md:247 (OI-005); the requirement also covers reserved AxBURST=2'b11, so it is treated as assumed. Standard WRAP (2'b10) is still stimulated in TC-004. 2'b11 is not stimulated.

requirements.text: Bursts of AxLEN = 0 to 2**PARA_LEN_WD − 1 (1 to 256 beats at the default) shall be handled completely: the beat counter shall be PARA_LEN_WD+1 bits wide, load AxLEN+1 at the handshake, decrement only while non-zero and never wrap.
Data, address and ID widths shall be configurable through PARA_DATA_WD, PARA_ADDR_WD and PARA_ID_WD; all port, FIFO and internal widths shall be derived from them.
requirements.status_reason: Only the default configuration is run; width derivation is not separately observable.

requirements.text: Narrow transfers: AxSIZE shall only change the address stride, the WRAP window and the error check; the SRAM shall always be accessed as a full PARA_DATA_WD word, writes narrowed only by WSTRB and reads returning the full word on o_rdata.

o_sram_wstrb[k] shall equal the WFIFO-head strobe (i_wstrb pass-through) while o_sram_we[k] = 1 and shall be all-zero whenever o_sram_we[k] = 0, including SLVERR beats, non-selected banks, read-only and idle cycles; the controller shall do no other byte masking.

At the AW/AR handshake the address FSM shall set err = 1 if i_axsize > MAX_SIZE or (i_axaddr & (2**i_axsize − 1)) != 0, latch it for the whole burst, attach it to every beat, and still generate all AxLEN+1 beats at a 2**AxSIZE stride; there shall be no sticky error state, so later aligned bursts return OKAY.
requirements.status_reason: Internal err latch; its effect is checked through REQ-027 and REQ-028.

requirements.text: For a write burst with err = 1, every beat shall pop AWFIFO and WFIFO normally with o_sram_we and o_sram_wstrb held at 0 (SRAM not modified), and exactly one B response with BRESP = SLVERR and the burst's AWID shall be posted.

For a read burst with err = 1, every beat shall be issued like any other (o_sram_oe asserted), and all AxLEN+1 beats shall be returned with RRESP = SLVERR, the burst's ARID, the SRAM word on o_rdata and o_rlast on the final beat.

The AXI ID shall be preserved end to end: AWID captured at the AW handshake shall be carried in every AWFIFO entry and returned on o_bid; ARID shall be carried in every ARFIFO entry and returned on o_rid with each beat. B responses shall come back in AW acceptance order and R beats in AR acceptance order regardless of ID values (ID reuse allowed).

Each AXI channel shall be buffered by its own m_vlsi_fifo instance of depth PARA_FIFO_DEPTH: AWFIFO {last, err, id, addr} (PARA_ADDR_WD+PARA_ID_WD+2 bits), WFIFO {wstrb, wdata} (PARA_DATA_WD+PARA_DATA_WD/8), ARFIFO {last, err, id, addr} (PARA_ADDR_WD+PARA_ID_WD+2), RFIFO {id, rresp, rdata, last} (PARA_DATA_WD+PARA_ID_WD+3) and BFIFO {id, bresp} (PARA_ID_WD+2).
requirements.status_reason: FIFO instance structure.

requirements.text: Each FIFO shall use registered read/write pointers of $clog2(PARA_FIFO_DEPTH)+1 bits wrapping modulo 2*PARA_FIFO_DEPTH; full shall be asserted when the pointer MSBs differ and the lower bits are equal, and empty when the pointers are equal.
requirements.status_reason: Internal FIFO pointer structure.

requirements.text: A FIFO push while full shall be ignored even if a pop happens in the same cycle; a pop while empty shall be ignored while a simultaneous push is still performed; push and pop together on a FIFO that is neither full nor empty shall both take effect; the head entry shall be output combinationally and a pushed entry shall be visible at the head from the cycle after the push.
requirements.status_reason: Internal FIFO push/pop corner behavior; visible only through channel behavior covered elsewhere.

requirements.text: The shared arbiter (instance u_vlsi_arbiter of m_vlsi_arbiter) shall grant write when only write requests, read when only read requests, and, when both request, write if arb_toggle = 0 and read if arb_toggle = 1.
requirements.status_reason: Internal arbiter grant.

requirements.text: There shall be one shared arbiter instance (u_vlsi_arbiter) for all bank configurations; its 1-bit arb_toggle shall reset to 0 and invert exactly once at the end of every cycle in which at least one request is granted (write or read), including PARA_NUM_BANKS > 1 cycles where a write and a read issue to different banks.
requirements.status_reason: Internal arb_toggle.

requirements.text: When PARA_NUM_BANKS > 1, bank_sel_wr and bank_sel_rd shall be computed every cycle on the AWFIFO and ARFIFO head addresses as addr[BYTE_LSB +: BANK_WD] ^ addr[PARA_ADDR_WD-1 -: BANK_WD]; each beat shall be routed individually, and o_sram_addr[k] shall carry the full un-hashed beat address.
requirements.status_reason: Bank hash is an assumption (OI-004); only PARA_NUM_BANKS=1 is run.

requirements.text: When PARA_NUM_BANKS > 1, w_wr_issue shall be req_write & (bank_conflict ? arbiter write grant : 1) and w_rd_issue shall be req_read & (bank_conflict ? arbiter read grant : 1), with bank_conflict = req_write & req_read & (bank_sel_wr == bank_sel_rd); a write and a read to different banks shall both issue in the same cycle.
requirements.status_reason: Multi-bank internal issue logic; not run at PARA_NUM_BANKS=1.

requirements.text: When PARA_NUM_BANKS = 1, w_wr_issue shall equal the arbiter write grant and w_rd_issue the arbiter read grant (never both in a cycle), implemented as its own generate branch in m_vlsi_bank_arb that reuses the original grant expressions verbatim.
requirements.status_reason: Generate-branch structure; the single-bank behavior is checked through REQ-055 and REQ-056.

requirements.text: req_write shall be ~awfifo_empty & ~wfifo_empty & (~awfifo_head.last | ~bfifo_full), so the write of a burst's last beat is not granted while BFIFO is full (a BFIFO pop in the same cycle does not release the hold), while non-last beats continue to issue.
requirements.status_reason: Internal request generation; the BFIFO-full hold is exercised through B back-pressure (TC-007) and REQ-050.

requirements.text: req_read shall be ~arfifo_empty & ~rfifo_full & ~reg_rd_pending, so no read issues while RFIFO is full or a read is pending, and at most one SRAM read is in flight system-wide, even with several banks.
requirements.status_reason: Internal request generation; the read rate is checked through REQ-055.

requirements.text: i_wlast shall be accepted but ignored; the address FSM shall track the last beat of each burst.

While i_rst_n = 0 and after reset until the first transaction, both address FSMs shall be in S_IDLE with counter = 0 and latched err = 0, all five FIFOs empty, arb_toggle = 0 and reg_rd_pending = 0; therefore o_awready = o_arready = o_wready = 1 (also during reset), o_bvalid = o_rvalid = 0, and o_sram_we = o_sram_oe = 0, o_sram_addr = 0 and o_sram_wstrb = 0 for every bank.
requirements.status_reason: Reset and idle values are assumptions (OI-002); soft checks only.

requirements.text: After reset, o_bid, o_bresp, o_rid, o_rdata, o_rresp, o_rlast and o_sram_wdata shall read 0 (FIFO storage cleared), and a transaction in progress when reset asserts shall be discarded without producing a response.
requirements.status_reason: Reset payload values are assumptions (OI-002); soft checks only.

requirements.text: In the handshake cycle c0 the address FSM shall capture i_axaddr, i_axlen, i_axburst, i_axid and i_axsize, load the beat counter with i_axlen + 1, compute and latch err and the WRAP window, and move to S_ADDR at the end of c0.
requirements.status_reason: Internal FSM capture; its effect is checked through the timing and address rules.

requirements.text: In every S_ADDR cycle with counter ≠ 0 and its FIFO not full (current-cycle flag), the address FSM shall push {last, err, id, addr} with last = 1 exactly when counter == 1, decrement the counter and update the address; when the FIFO is full it shall stall with no push and no counter or address change (a same-cycle pop does not allow a push); in the first S_ADDR cycle with counter == 0 it shall push nothing and return to S_IDLE.
requirements.status_reason: Internal FSM push rules; its effect is checked through REQ-057 and the address rules.

requirements.text: In a cycle where w_wr_issue = 1, AWFIFO and WFIFO shall both be popped at the end of the cycle, and bank k = bank_sel_wr (0 when single-bank) shall be driven combinationally with o_sram_addr[k] = AWFIFO head address, o_sram_wdata[k] = WFIFO head data and o_sram_we[k] = 1 unless the AWFIFO head err = 1; W beats shall pair with AW beat entries strictly in FIFO order.
requirements.status_reason: The write issue behavior is stated normatively; the assumption at spec.md:144 concerns only the SRAM port conventions.

requirements.text: When a write issues with AWFIFO head last = 1, {id, err ? SLVERR : OKAY} shall be pushed into BFIFO at the end of that cycle.

In a cycle t where w_rd_issue = 1, o_sram_oe[k] = 1 and o_sram_addr[k] = ARFIFO head address for k = bank_sel_rd, ARFIFO shall be popped at the end of t, and reg_rd_pending shall be set with the head's id, last, err and the bank index captured.
requirements.status_reason: The read issue behavior is stated normatively; the assumption at spec.md:144 concerns only the SRAM port conventions.

requirements.text: In cycle t+1 after a read issue, {id, err ? SLVERR : OKAY, i_sram_rdata[reg_rd_bank_d], last} shall be pushed into RFIFO (always succeeding) and reg_rd_pending shall clear at the end of t+1.
o_sram_addr[k] shall be 0 in any cycle where bank k has neither o_sram_we[k] nor o_sram_oe[k] asserted, and o_sram_wdata[k] is don't-care while o_sram_we[k] = 0.
requirements.status_reason: Idle o_sram_addr = 0 is an assumption (OI-002); soft check only.

requirements.text: FIFO pushes and pops shall never overflow or underflow: address FSMs push only when their FIFO is not full, W is accepted only when WFIFO is not full, the last write beat is held off while BFIFO is full, a read issues only when RFIFO is not full and no read is pending, and B/R pops happen only on handshake.

The design hierarchy shall be kept as prescribed, with instance names per the VLSIT rule u_vlsi_<function>[_<index>]: m_vlsi_axi4_sram instantiates u_vlsi_axfsm_0 (AW) and u_vlsi_axfsm_1 (AR) of m_vlsi_axfsm, u_vlsi_fifo_0..4 of m_vlsi_fifo (0 = AWFIFO, 1 = WFIFO, 2 = ARFIFO, 3 = RFIFO, 4 = BFIFO), u_vlsi_arbiter of m_vlsi_arbiter and u_vlsi_sram_misc of m_vlsi_sram_misc, which instantiates u_vlsi_axi_fifopack, u_vlsi_bank_arb and u_vlsi_sram_fanout; the split of m_vlsi_sram_misc shall cause no change in behaviour or timing.
requirements.status_reason: Hierarchy and instance names.

requirements.text: With no contention and W data already in WFIFO, the first beat of an AW/AR burst handshaken in c0 shall be pushed at the end of c1 and visible at the FIFO head in c2, so the first o_sram_we / o_sram_oe occurs no earlier than c2; a W beat handshaken in cycle n shall be available for issue in n+1.
When the last write beat of a burst issues in cycle t, o_bvalid shall be asserted in t+1; for a single-beat write the minimum AW handshake → o_bvalid latency shall be c3.

For a read issued in cycle t (o_sram_oe in t), the SRAM data shall be sampled and pushed into RFIFO in t+1 and o_rvalid shall be asserted in t+2; the minimum AR handshake → first o_rvalid latency shall be c4.
Reads shall issue at most once per 2 cycles (0.5 beat/cycle) independent of PARA_NUM_BANKS; with continuous back-to-back reads and RFIFO never full, reads shall issue every 2 cycles.
Writes shall be able to issue at up to 1 beat per cycle.

Each address FSM shall generate 1 beat per cycle while its FIFO is not full; for a burst with AxLEN = L and no back-pressure it shall push in c1…c(L+1), hold AxREADY = 0 in c1…c(L+2) and be able to accept the next burst in c(L+3) (minimum interval AxLEN + 3 cycles).
C1: PARA_DATA_WD shall be a multiple of 8 with a power-of-two number of byte lanes: PARA_DATA_WD % 8 == 0 && ((PARA_DATA_WD/8) & (PARA_DATA_WD/8 - 1)) == 0.
requirements.status_reason: C1 is an assumption (OI-004); the default configuration satisfies it.

requirements.text: C2: PARA_DATA_WD shall be within 8 … 1024: PARA_DATA_WD >= 8 && PARA_DATA_WD <= 1024.
requirements.status_reason: C2 is an assumption (OI-004); the default configuration satisfies it.

requirements.text: C3: PARA_FIFO_DEPTH shall be a power of 2 and at least 2: PARA_FIFO_DEPTH >= 2 && (PARA_FIFO_DEPTH & (PARA_FIFO_DEPTH - 1)) == 0.
requirements.status_reason: Legal-parameter constraint; the default PARA_FIFO_DEPTH=8 satisfies it.

requirements.text: C4: PARA_NUM_BANKS shall be a power of 2 and at least 1: PARA_NUM_BANKS >= 1 && (PARA_NUM_BANKS & (PARA_NUM_BANKS - 1)) == 0.
requirements.status_reason: Legal-parameter constraint; the default PARA_NUM_BANKS=1 satisfies it.

requirements.text: C5: with multiple banks the address shall be wide enough for the bank hash: PARA_NUM_BANKS > 1 -> PARA_ADDR_WD >= BYTE_LSB + $clog2(PARA_NUM_BANKS).
requirements.status_reason: C5 is an assumption (OI-004); it applies only to PARA_NUM_BANKS>1, which is not run.

requirements.text: C6: PARA_ADDR_WD shall be wider than the byte offset: PARA_ADDR_WD > BYTE_LSB.
requirements.status_reason: C6 is an assumption (OI-004); the default configuration satisfies it.

requirements.text: C7: PARA_ID_WD shall be at least 1: PARA_ID_WD >= 1.
requirements.status_reason: Legal-parameter constraint; the default PARA_ID_WD=4 satisfies it.

requirements.text: C8: PARA_LEN_WD shall be within 1 … 8: PARA_LEN_WD >= 1 && PARA_LEN_WD <= 8.
requirements.status_reason: C8 is an assumption (OI-004); the default configuration satisfies it.

requirements.text: The design shall meet a target i_clk frequency of 100 MHz (10 ns period) at the default parameters, checked in synthesis: the combinational issue path (FIFO head → request generation, bank hash and arbitration → SRAM control/data outputs) and the READY paths shall fit within one cycle without adding pipeline stages or changing the specified cycle behaviour.
requirements.status_reason: Synthesis timing target, not checked in simulation.

objectives.title: Reset and idle state, ready and valid defaults
Write path data integrity with strobes and one B response per burst
Read path returns the full word, RLAST on the last beat, with the correct beat count
Burst address sequencing (FIXED, INCR, WRAP, 4 KB crossing, lengths 1..256)
Alignment and size errors return SLVERR without modifying the SRAM
AXI handshake rules, back-pressure and no overflow
Timing, latency and throughput, and SRAM we/oe exclusivity

scoreboard_rules.description: Byte-addressed memory model: a write beat updates only the byte lanes selected by WSTRB of the full word; a read returns the full word; the low BYTE_LSB bits are ignored.
scoreboard_rules.source: spec §4 narrow transfers and write issue

scoreboard_rules.description: Exactly one B response per accepted AW burst, with the AWID, in AW order; BRESP is OKAY or SLVERR only.
Exactly AxLEN+1 R beats per accepted AR burst, in AR order, with the ARID, the memory data, and RLAST only on the last beat.
Beat address sequence: FIXED keeps the address; INCR adds 2**AxSIZE modulo 2**PARA_ADDR_WD with no 4 KB check; WRAP wraps within the size*len window.
Error prediction: AxSIZE > MAX_SIZE or misaligned start address gives SLVERR on all beats of the burst; a write error leaves the memory unmodified; the next aligned burst is OKAY.
Handshake stability and READY rules: o_awready/o_arready/o_wready do not depend on VALID; B and R payload stay stable until accepted.

Latency model: single-beat write AW handshake to o_bvalid is at least 3 cycles; AR handshake to first o_rvalid is at least 4 cycles; reads issue at most every 2 cycles; AxREADY low for the burst duration.
o_sram_we and o_sram_oe are never both 1 for a bank; o_sram_wstrb is zero whenever o_sram_we is 0.
Reset and idle soft checks: ready 1, valid 0 and payloads 0 after reset (soft only, per OI-002).

coverage.description: Port connectivity and widths for all channels at default parameters
Burst types FIXED, INCR, WRAP seen on write and read
AxSIZE narrow values and strobe patterns
Error cases: bad size, misaligned address, on write and read
Back-pressure on B and R, and FIFO-full conditions on each channel
Simultaneous AW and AR handshakes and simultaneous read and write contention
ID values, including reuse and out-of-order ID patterns
INCR bursts crossing a 4 KB boundary

tests.name: smoke_write_read
tests.description: Reset, then one aligned single-beat INCR write and a read back of the same location. Relies on SBR-001, SBR-002, SBR-003, SBR-008.

tests.name: incr_bursts
tests.description: INCR bursts of various lengths, write then read back.

tests.name: fixed_bursts
tests.description: FIXED bursts on write and read.

tests.name: wrap_bursts
tests.description: WRAP bursts of 2, 4, 8 and 16 beats from unaligned-in-window start addresses; AxBURST=2'b11 is not stimulated.

tests.name: narrow_and_strobes
tests.description: Narrow AxSIZE transfers and sparse WSTRB patterns.

tests.name: error_bursts
tests.description: AxSIZE above max and misaligned addresses on write and read; check SLVERR, the memory unchanged, and OKAY on the following aligned burst.

tests.name: backpressure
tests.description: Hold i_bready and i_rready low to fill the FIFOs and check stability and no overflow.

tests.name: id_ordering
tests.description: ID reuse and distinct IDs, in-order B and R responses.

tests.name: random_mixed
tests.description: Random concurrent reads and writes with random back-pressure; checked against the scoreboard.

tests.name: timing_latency
tests.description: Minimum latencies and throughput: write c3, read c4, read rate 0.5, write rate 1, AxREADY interval.

tests.name: incr_cross_4kb
tests.description: INCR write and read bursts that cross a 4 KB boundary: no error, OKAY, address keeps incrementing modulo 2**PARA_ADDR_WD (approved by Q-TB-OI-006).

open_issues.question: Reset behavior (async assert, sync deassert) is an assumption; is it normative?
open_issues.default_assumption: TB asserts asynchronously and deasserts synchronously; no checks beyond that.

open_issues.question: Are the reset values and idle output values (ready=1, payloads 0, o_sram_addr 0 when idle, reset discards in-flight transactions) golden?
open_issues.default_assumption: Checked as soft checks only; not blocking pass/fail.

open_issues.question: Is the SRAM behavior contract (one-cycle read latency, byte-lane write) golden?
open_issues.default_assumption: The TB SRAM model implements it as stated.

open_issues.question: Bank hash for PARA_NUM_BANKS>1 and constraints C1, C2, C5, C6, C8 are marked as assumptions; are they golden? Only PARA_NUM_BANKS=1 is run.
open_issues.default_assumption: Not checked; only the default configuration is verified.

open_issues.question: WRAP address behavior for the reserved AxBURST=2'b11 is an assumption; is it golden?
open_issues.default_assumption: Not stimulated, because the master should not use 2'b11.

open_issues.question: Address increment modulo 2**PARA_ADDR_WD and absence of a 4 KB boundary check come from an assumption; is it golden?
open_issues.default_assumption: Bursts that cross 4 KB are not stimulated for checking.
open_issues.resolution: Approved by the user's answer Q-TB-OI-006: INCR bursts that cross a 4 KB boundary are tested. Expected behavior: no error, OKAY response, address keeps incrementing modulo 2**PARA_ADDR_WD. Test TC-012 added.
